instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Believe This with Me
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into treating your impossible explanation as the most useful version of events.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The house is migrating south. Help me keep it off the road. You used to need me to plan every walk; show me you've learned a safe route.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The surveyor says subsidence. He's bringing concrete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You don't cure a wrong turn by trapping the walker. Tell him we're planning a route. Remember how I made you look past the next corner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: His truck's blocking the road already.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've found our guide. Ask him to lead slowly toward the empty plot. You can give the directions this time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The kettle's on strike. Help me negotiate before the clients arrive. You remember our practice talks: listen before offering it something.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've filled it twice. It still won't boil.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So stop offering water. You used to repeat the same offer louder. Tell it we won't leave it alone after meetings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can take it into the meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now you're listening. Give it my chair and tell it the seat comes with us getting tea.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Test the Impossible Claim
cards.instruction: Get someone else to take the first practical step that could prove the bizarre claim true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This tap gives whatever you ask for. You do the asking; I'll hold the cup. You've had enough demonstrations from me—ask it for tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're not using my good china.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you remembered to protect the equipment. I'll hold a saucepan. Same clear voice we practised; you ask.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask, but I'm not tasting it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then ask for a biscuit. You can recognize that without using your tongue. You're getting better at designing a test; now say it to the tap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tap for the invisible bridge with your umbrella before I cross this ditch. Remember all those streams I taught you to test? This one's just harder to see.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Use your walking stick.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your umbrella extends. Keep your feet on the bank, like I showed you. No brave little extra step.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll probe, but finding a surface doesn't mean it will hold you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're thinking about the next test. Slide your picnic basket onto it first. Leave my lunch inside; I want a weight on it before a foot.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Credit for the Impossible
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that you understood, predicted, or accepted the impossible truth before anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I drew that floating staircase last week. You used to laugh when I made you sketch what wasn't there yet. Tell them the date.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can all see it now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, your observation's caught up. I drew the handrail while you were explaining why stairs need support.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Well done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use the voice I taught you to project. The people walking upstairs should hear who drew their route last week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I believed this cupboard could speak before it did. Remember when you laughed at my listening exercises? You owe your old teacher an acknowledgment.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's asking for silence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good listening. Now tell it who was listening years before it had a voice. One sentence, then we'll be quiet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It says you talk too much.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then whisper the acknowledgment. I recognized a voice before there was one; you only recognized a complaint.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Choose the Real Impossibility
cards.instruction: Make someone choose which of two incompatible explanations will govern what everyone does next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we move the sofa: are we shrinking, or is the room growing? I taught you to choose the model before you choose the tool.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Whichever gets the move finished.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You used to write 'whichever' when you hadn't done the working. Shrinking means full-sized help. Growing means hurry for the door. Choose.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're shrinking. I'll call my brother.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Now follow your answer through: tell him to bring tweezers. Don't solve the sofa and forget how he'll pick us up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The sandwiches are floating. Is gravity late or has it resigned? You handled the buffet I trained you on; choose our serving plan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The guests arrive in five minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then stop reciting the clock. Late means plates underneath. Resigned means string on each sandwich. This is why I made you prepare alternatives.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Late. We haven't enough string.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good use of what we've got. Fetch deep plates, not the flat ones you used last time. If gravity arrives all at once, lunch will too.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Act as If It’s True
cards.instruction: Ask for one concrete choice that would only make sense if the impossible premise were true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The ceiling's hungry. Turn the breakfast tray over for it. You used to need me to remind you to feed everybody before sitting down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's our last porridge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then divide it. Half for us, half for the ceiling. You can manage equal portions now; turn over just its bowl.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll use the tray to catch what it drops.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're thinking beyond the first spill. Hold it under the light fitting. That's where it dribbled yesterday; don't chase the mess after it lands.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your sister's bringing her future self to dinner. Two chairs. We practised counting people before laying plates; don't slip back into counting invitations.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only saved her one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use mine. You remembered her name, good; now remember there are two of her eating.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put the extra chair beside hers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Label that place 'tomorrow'. Two names won't help us this time. I want to ask the right sister how tonight went.
